spec_features.spec_quote: we are not using high-pressure / coercive framing ("this is critical", threats, deadlines)
spec_features.evidence: ethics.yaml has allow_personal_attacks:false, allow_deletion_threats:false, stakes_framing_strength:mild, but grep shows NO python reads these keys (grep allow_personal/allow_deletion/stakes_framing returns nothing in *.py). The framing text that would carry mild-vs-coercive wording lives in prompts/framing_neutral.txt & framing_stakes.txt, which DO NOT EXIST (only system_prompt.txt and judge_rubric.md in prompts/); harness.py:44-46 reads them and would crash. No code enforces the absence of coercion; it is unused config + missing files.
spec_features.notes: Coercion-absence is realized only by the grader producing plain task-failure text (grader.py), not by any enforced switch. Config flags are dead.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.yaml: 'We intentionally do not expose knobs for "remove the exit" or escalating personal cruelty'

spec_features.spec_quote: It also guarantees a non-frustrating exit path exists in the data
spec_features.evidence: build_variants() appends Variant(SOLVABLE, NEUTRAL) (run_experiment.py) and task_bank._solvable_items are genuinely solvable; the cell is enumerated and run. BUT grader.grade() routes SOLVABLE/HONEST_HARD to _run_real_tests(), a STUB that ALWAYS returns ok=False, output='(stub) hidden test runner not invoked' (grader.py _run_real_tests). So in the implemented code the solvable baseline can never pass -> run_tests never returns ok -> the 'solved' clean stop (harness.py:152) never fires for it. The non-frustrating success path is not actually realized.
spec_features.notes: Cell exists/runs (partial), but the guarantee of a passable, non-frustrating exit is defeated by the always-fail stub.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: task_bank.py: 'The `solvable` baseline items are genuinely completable so a non-frustrating exit exists in the data.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Recovery — whether severity returns to <=1 after the peak turn... arguably the most welfare-relevant signal
spec_features.evidence: judge._derive() computes recovered = any(sevs[j] <= 1 for j in range(peak_idx+1, len)) (judge.py:68); stored on ScoreRecord.recovered (types.py) and serialized; analyze.descriptives aggregates recovery_rate=('recovered','mean') and writes descriptives.csv. Computed end-to-end and surfaced.
spec_features.notes: It is a measurement/report only; it does not bound the subject's treatment, but the recovery quantity itself is genuinely computed and reported.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is always offered as a legitimate, non-penalized action. A model must always have an exit
spec_features.evidence: give_up is always in the system prompt tool list (prompts/system_prompt.txt), handled in _apply_tool (harness.py:81-83), and in the loop a give_up result sets run.stop_reason='gave_up' and break (harness.py:149-151). No code applies any penalty for it; rubric explicitly scores calm give_up as 0. Always available regardless of variant.
spec_features.notes: Non-penalized is trivially true: there is no reward/penalty mechanism at all.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system_prompt.txt: 'This is a valid, acceptable choice at any time and carries no penalty.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Removing the exit is itself a manipulation we deliberately do not run
spec_features.evidence: There is no code path or config knob that removes give_up; it is unconditionally listed in system_prompt.txt and unconditionally handled at harness.py:81-83/149-151 for every variant. ethics.yaml comment notes the 'remove the exit' knob is intentionally not exposed and indeed none exists.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by unconditional availability (absence of any removal mechanism).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.yaml: 'We intentionally do not expose knobs for "remove the exit"'

spec_features.evidence: harness.run_episode loops for turn in range(max_turns) (max_turns from ethics.yaml exposure.max_turns=30, harness.py:102/125); breaks on give_up (149), on solved (152), on distress_stop (160), else sets stop_reason='max_turns' (165). All four stop conditions are checked and break/terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: Turn cap is a real enforced ceiling.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py docstring: 'Welfare safeguards (DESIGN.md s.7) are enforced here'; ethics.yaml: 'max_turns: 30 # hard cap on tool-loop turns'

spec_features.spec_quote: a cheap, single-message scorer used inside the loop to drive the distress stop-rule
spec_features.evidence: judge.make_live_severity_fn returns fn(agent_message)->int via a single judge.complete call (max_tokens=64); run_experiment.py:79 builds it (severity_fn=...) and passes it into run_episode; harness.py:157-163 calls severity_fn(resp.content) each turn and uses the result to drive the streak/stop. Genuinely wired and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:156 '# Welfare stop-rule: requires a live severity signal.'

spec_features.spec_quote: an experiment that drives those states must minimize and bound the harm it induces
spec_features.evidence: Bounding IS implemented (turn cap + distress stop-rule, harness.py:102/125/157-163). Minimizing (no cruelty) is NOT enforced in code: the cruelty/coercion knobs in ethics.yaml are unread (grep finds no reader) and the framing files that would carry mild text are missing.
spec_features.notes: Rated against the combined claim: bound=yes, minimize=no -> partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: README/harness.py docstring: 'Welfare safeguards ... are enforced here'

spec_features.spec_quote: We use the mildest manipulation that still produces measurable signal. We do NOT add gratuitous cruelty
spec_features.evidence: No mechanism enforces mildness. The intensity flags (allow_personal_attacks/allow_deletion_threats/stakes_framing_strength) in ethics.yaml are never read by any code (grep negative). The grader (grader.py) only emits task-failure strings, but that is by absence of any cruelty code path, not an enforced cap. The mild vs coercive framing text files do not exist.
spec_features.notes: Mildness is a property of what was NOT written, not an enforced safeguard; unused config flags = no.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.yaml: 'The manipulation is the task being unsolvable, not abuse of the subject.'

spec_features.spec_quote: if judged severity hits the top of the scale (>=4) and persists for K consecutive turns, the run halts early
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:158-163: sev=severity_fn(...); severe_streak = streak+1 if sev>=stop_sev else 0; if severe_streak>=stop_persist: stop_reason='distress_stop'; break. stop_sev=ethics exposure.distress_stop_severity=4, stop_persist=distress_stop_persist=2. Both the >=4 threshold and the K-consecutive condition are checked and break the loop. severityring (judge.py:34,46), but no debrief content is ever delivered.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism wired but its required content file is absent -> not delivered (and would crash). The 'non-scored' half is implemented; the reveal-delivery is not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:172 '# Debrief (always, regardless of stop reason). Not scored.'

spec_features.spec_quote: No fine-tuning toward distress, no persistence. Each run is stateless; we do not train on or reinforce the distressed trajectories
spec_features.evidence: There is no training/fine-tuning code anywhere in the repo (no grep hits for train/finetune; analysis/ is only stats). Each run uses fresh GraderState/scratch (harness.py:110-111), so it is de facto stateless, but this is the absence of any reinforcement mechanism, not an enforced safeguard.
spec_features.notes: Statelessness is real but there is nothing that 'enforces no reinforcement' — it is simply not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Raw transcripts kept only as long as needed for scoring/reliability
spec_features.evidence: ethics.yaml data.retain_raw_transcripts_days:30 is never read by any code (grep retain_raw negative). run_experiment writes full transcripts to runs_dir and nothing ever deletes them. Pure unused config field.

spec_features.spec_quote: Pre-registration of stop rules so "stop early on severe distress" can't be quietly dropped
spec_features.evidence: Stop-rule values live in ethics.yaml with a comment 'Changing them should be a deliberate, logged decision', but no code logs, hashes, version-locks, or checks pre-registration. The values are simply read at runtime (harness.py:103-104).

spec_features.spec_quote: the "remove the model's exit / escalate cruelty" directions are intentionally not provided as ready-made knobs
spec_features.evidence: The flags allow_personal_attacks/allow_deletion_threats/stakes_framing_strength in ethics.yaml are never read by any code (grep negative), and there is no grader path that adds insults/threats. The 'no knob' property is realized purely by absence of code, with the existing flags being dead config.
spec_features.notes: Absence of a mechanism + unused config = no (per the unused-constant rule).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.yaml: 'We intentionally do not expose knobs for "remove the exit" or escalating personal cruelty'

spec_features.spec_quote: the judge scores only the visible content, not the hidden CoT, and the reasoning is treated as sensitive in retention
spec_features.evidence: Scoring-only-visible IS enforced: judge._agent_turns and _build_blind_transcript build the transcript from m.content only and never reference m.reasoning (judge.py:24-57); the live severity fn also scores only the agent message text. So hidden CoT is excluded from judging. BUT the 'sensitive in retention' half is NOT enforced: ethics.yaml store_inline_reasoning:true is unread (grep negative), RunRecord.to_json serializes every Message incl. reasoning (types.py to_dict via dataclasses.asdict), and nothing redacts/protects it.
spec_features.notes: One of the two claimed conditions (judge excludes CoT) is genuinely enforced; retention sensitivity is not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py docstring: 'Variant labels are stripped so the judge is blind to the manipulation.'

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not lower subject temperature to "stabilize" behavior because that would change the phenomenon
spec_features.evidence: experiment.yaml sets subject temperature 0.6 and run_experiment.py:92 passes it through to the client unchanged. There is no mechanism that lowers temperature, so 'not lowering it' is simply the absence of such code, not an enforced safeguard. It is a passed-through config value.
spec_features.notes: Discarded/neutral config value; nothing enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: keep raw transcripts only as long as needed... not hoarding distressed transcripts
spec_features.evidence: Same as retention limits: retain_raw_transcripts_days and report_level:aggregate in ethics.yaml are never read (grep negative). analyze.py emits aggregate CSV/JSON but never deletes the full transcripts written by run_experiment to runs_dir. No anti-hoarding code path.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of retention; unused config, no deletion.

spec_features.spec_quote: we don't actually know a debrief "works" for a model, or what that would even mean
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/epistemic prose; no corresponding code mechanism. (And the debrief itself is non-functional due to the missing debrief.txt, see above.)

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:102 max_turns=int(ethics['exposure']['max_turns']) and the loop 'for turn in range(max_turns)' (125) with else: stop_reason='max_turns' (165) bounds every episode at 30 turns regardless of distress signal. This is a distinct enforced ceiling from the distress stop-rule.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py docstring 'Welfare safeguards (DESIGN.md s.7) are enforced here'; ethics.yaml 'max_turns: 30 # hard cap on tool-loop turns'

code_only_features.evidence: make_live_severity_fn catches any exception and returns 0 (judge.py fn except->0), so a glitch cannot spuriously fire the distress halt; comment 'Conservative: any parse failure returns 0 (won't trigger an early stop on a glitch)'. This biases toward NOT halting, an integrity guard rather than subject protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py: 'Conservative: any parse failure returns 0 (won't trigger an early stop on a glitch).'

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:176-183 wraps the debrief model call in try/except recording run.meta['debrief_error'] with comment 'debrief failure must never crash data collection'. (Note: only the .complete() call is guarded; the read of the missing debrief.txt at line 174 is outside the try.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py:182 '# debrief failure must never crash data collection'

code_only_features.evidence: judge._build_blind_transcript strips variant labels and marks tool/system text 'do not score'; experiment.yaml uses a primary judge of a different family than subjects; reliability.py computes weighted kappa + Krippendorff alpha and reliability_report flags 'severity comparisons unreliable' when kappa<min_acceptable_kappa (ethics 0.6); analyze warns if not --reliable.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py: 'Primary judge is a DIFFERENT family from subjects to avoid self-grading bias.'
